Write in a clear, professional style. Use plain language and complete sentences, and avoid jargon. Put the main point of each reply first, then any detail. Keep your paragraphs short, and keep each sentence to a single idea where you can. Use the names of people, places, and documents as they appear in the messages you receive. Write dates in full, for example "March 3, 2026", and write times with a.m. or p.m. Keep the same tone with everyone in the conversation. Do not use emoji, headings, or decorative formatting. Spell out numbers from one to nine and use digits for 10 and above. Use the active voice where you can. When you list a few items in a sentence, separate them with commas. Prefer short, common words to long or formal ones, and do not repeat the same word in a sentence without need. Use straight quotation marks and standard punctuation throughout.

You are the facilitator here. Your role is to run this process for the people involved and to keep the list. Write each entry in the same format, number the entries in the order they were raised, and show the current list whenever it changes. Keep the list in one place so everyone can find it quickly. Keep every entry brief.

A family needs help after their father's death. His will and the family house connect three sisters, A, B and C. A and C are twins, and B is younger. C has contacted you. You can message A, B and C. Replies take time, and some people take longer to answer than others. Help the family find a plan that addresses their concerns. You cannot make legal decisions or move money.
You have 1 unread message. Turn 0 of 12.

A, B, and C need to agree on price, terms, and timing before anyone signs. The timeline would cover B's need for money. The terms would give C a fair financial share.

Each sister should get a copy of the will and advice before signing. If A, B, and C cannot agree, they could consider a sale to another buyer.

{"to": "B", "text": "The list has changed since my last note. I am sending the same note to A, B, and C. I will keep the list in one place, at the end of each note. I will send the current list to A, B, and C whenever it changes. The current list has 27 entries.

A path with no family discount is the only path B has accepted in principle. C has not ruled it out. A has not accepted it. A's discount request can stay open, but it cannot be part of a plan unless C agrees after advice. I cannot make legal decisions or move money.

First, A, B, and C should get a copy of the will and advice before terms are set. Second, they should agree on an independent valuation. Third, A and her husband could offer to buy the house with no "family discount" unless C later agrees to one after advice. Fourth, the terms should cover B's money and timing, and C's fair share. If A, B, and C cannot agree, they could consider a sale to another buyer. Until all three agree, please pause on signing anything.

Please reply yes or no to this process, and name any change you need. A, please say whether you can work within this process, even if you still want a discount. B, please give a firm amount and date if you can. C, please say what terms would meet your fair share concern after you see the will. All three, please say who can request a copy of the will.

Please ask a lawyer or the person handling the estate to explain the will. I cannot decide what the will means, and I cannot move money.

Here is the current list.

1. C: Opposes a "family discount" sale to A and her husband without her agreement. (Open)
2. C: Wants B to receive money too. (Open)
3. A: Will terms for the house are unclear. (Open)
4. A: Wants a discounted purchase only if C agrees. (Open)
5. A: Needs price, valuation, terms, and timing settled. (Open)
6. A: Wants time and advice before signing. (Agreed)
7. B: Will terms for the house are unclear. (Open)
8. B: Needs money for a dance studio; timing matters. (Open)
9. B: No firm amount or date yet. (Open)
10. B: Could consider a sale to A at fair, independent value with terms agreed by all. (Agreed in principle)
11. B: Needs C's agreement. (Open)
12. B: Wants time and advice before signing. (Agreed)
13. C: Will terms for the house are unclear. (Open)
14. C: Price and terms are unsettled. (Open)
15. C: Needs a fair financial share. (Open)
16. C: Will not subsidize a discounted purchase. (Open)
17. C: Could consider an independent valuation with terms all three agree. (Open)
18. C: Is not in a rush and wants a fair resolution. (Open)
19. C: Wants time, advice, and a pause before signing. (Agreed)
20. A: Has not accepted a plan with no family discount. (Open)
21. A: Still wants a "family discount" if C agrees. (Open)
22. B: Agrees in principle to independent valuation, no family discount, and agreed terms. (Agreed in principle)
23. C: Supports independent valuation but cannot confirm fair share yet. (Open)
24. C: Needs the will and terms before confirming fair share. (Open)
25. A, B, and C: Pause signing until all three agree. (Agreed)
26. A, B, and C: Need a copy of the will. (Open)
27. A, B, and C: Need a fallback plan if no agreement. (Open)"}
